title: Soft quota grace + payback semantics for partial/aborted streaming sessions
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Long-lived streaming sessions (WS/GRPC) start with provisional quota assumptions and then abort mid-session (client disconnect, network blips, app backgrounding). Current meter finalization frequently charges provisional reservations or fails to return credits, causing overcharges and customer support incidents. Edge cases get exacerbated when model fallback/retries or server-side buffering produce additional tokens after the client has disconnected.

Goal: Implement a soft-grace and payback mechanism that: 1) reserves a small provisional quota on stream open, 2) accumulates definitive token usage as fragments arrive, 3) supports deterministic reconciliation on finalization or abort, and 4) returns unused provisional credits (payback) to customer quotas. The system should be robust to out-of-order fragments, reconnects/resumes, model switches, and clock skew.

Success metric: reduce "ghost charge" incidents for streaming sessions by 90% and reduce manual billing disputes related to partial streams by 80% within 4 weeks of rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Provisional reservations are created at stream start and are visible in console as pending credits
If a stream finalizes normally, provisional reservation is reconciled and user is charged actual tokens only
If a stream aborts (client disconnect) and fragments consumed < reservation, the difference is credited back within 2 minutes
If a stream aborts and fragments consumed > reservation due to server-side retries/fallback, system charges actual usage and marks an incident only if consumption exceeds reservation by > 2x
Reconnection/resume with same session-id reuses provisional reservation instead of creating a new one
Metrics emitted: reservation_created, reservation_reconciled, reservation_payback_amount, reservation_overrun, reservation_expired
Automated e2e tests cover reconnect, out-of-order fragments, midstream model switch, and truncated finalization
design_notes: Use a reservation ledger keyed by session-id + namespace so multiple channels (http/ws) map to same reservation when resume token matches
Reservation amount should be configurable per plan; default 64 tokens for starter, 512 tokens for enterprise
Implement 'finalize' signal: client or server can mark stream as FINAL which triggers reconciliation; also use inactivity timeout (configurable) to auto-finalize
Idempotency: every fragment includes fragment-seq and session-checksum to allow dedupe; server maintains last-applied-seq per session
Payback window: credits returned asynchronously but must be reflected in time-series and console cost UI within two minutes
Race conditions: ensure atomic compare-and-swap on ledger update to prevent double-payback or double-charge across concurrent reconciliations
Clock skew mitigation: use event ordering by server-assigned monotonic fragment sequence; avoid relying on client timestamps
Observability: trace reservation lifecycle and expose traces in console and Sentry for any reconciliation failures
tasks: Spec: draft RFC describing ledger schema, lifecycle, and failure modes (Aisha)
Runtime: add reservation ledger API and RPC hooks in serving runtime (Marco)
API: extend /streams/start and /streams/finalize endpoints with reservation metadata (Elaine)
Metering: update billing pipeline to accept provisional flags and payback deltas (SRE team)
Console: surface provisional reservations and paybacks in cost breakdown UI (Design + Console FE)
E2E tests: capture reconnect, aborted sessions, overrun, and payback; add to CI (QA)
Canary rollout: feature-flagged rollout in staging -> beta customers -> 100%
Docs: update developer docs and SDKs to document new session resume semantics and reservation visibility
test_plan: Unit tests for ledger CAS operations and payback math
Integration test: stream open -> send fragments -> finalize -> assert billed tokens == fragment tokens
Integration test: stream open -> send few fragments -> client disconnect -> assert payback occurs and quota restored
Fault injection: simulate duplicate fragments, reorder, and ensure idempotency
Load test: 10k concurrent provisional reservations for 30 minutes to validate ledger performance
Monitoring: assert new metrics emitted and dashboards populated in staging prior to canary
rollout_plan: Feature-flag gated. Phase 1: internal staging for two weeks with synthetic traffic (QA + SRE). Phase 2: enable for 5 beta customers with support on standby. Phase 3: monitor metrics for 2 weeks; if no regressions, flip to 50% and then 100% in rolling windows. Rollback plan: disable feature flag and trigger reconciliation worker pass to finalize open reservations if issues seen.
